title: Adaptive window synchronization failure and fallback playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
During a capacity ramp on 2026-03-11 we observed intermittent, reproducible episodes where continuous batch formation stopped accepting new requests for 2–8 seconds. These "quiet windows" caused severe tail latency spikes (p99.9 from baseline ~750ms to ~2.8s) and uneven request distribution across tenants, resulting in visible degradation for high-traffic customers.

Detection and impact:
- First alert: 2026-03-11 09:42 UTC (routing service errors from long blocking in the batch coordinator).
- Affected fleets: hosted inference region-us-west-2, model family: open-ggml-13b and some quantized variants.
- Customer-visible symptoms: slow streaming starts, timeouts on commodity PLG endpoints, and elevated error budgets for two customers (investigation opened by SRE).
- Throughput drop: up to 12% for affected partitions during incidents.

Timeline (condensed):
- 2026-03-11 09:42: alert fires.
- 09:47: SRE escalates to runtime on-call.
- 09:54: on-call reproduces locally with loadgen and confirms deterministic pauses in batch acceptance.
- 10:30: rollback of recent heuristic (PR #8347) applied to a small canary; immediate improvement observed.
- 11:10: full rollback to runtime-1.21 for impacted fleet; incidents clear.

Root cause analysis (summary):
- The regression was introduced by a change to the adaptive-window backpressure heuristic (runtime-1.22, PR #8347). The heuristic attempted to be more conservative when token-length estimates changed rapidly by pinning window timers to a slot reservation token. Under mixed workloads with sudden bursts of short-context requests, timer drift combined with a logic path that avoided emitting a fallback batch if the estimated occupancy was below a tightened threshold, leading to temporary "synchronization gaps" where no batch would be emitted until an external event reset the timer.
- Secondary contributor: a subtle race in the slot-allocator fast-path where cancellation of stale reservations did not wake the coordinator when the cache hit heuristic returned true for the first request in a slot. This dependency between two optimizations (conservative timer + cache-hit fast-path) created a composite failure mode not covered by existing unit tests.

Why this was missed by tests: 
- Existing unit tests covered single-feature regressions (timer behavior and cancellation) in isolation but not their interaction under high variability of request sizes and KV cache hit patterns. Load tests used relatively steady request-size distributions; the pathological mixed-burst pattern was absent.

Temporary mitigation applied:
- Immediate rollback of PR #8347 (adaptive-window heuristic) to runtime-1.21 on the affected fleets.
- Short-term operator knob added to disable cache-hit fast-path waking optimization (feature flag off) while we investigate.

Action items (owners and due dates):
1) Short-term: Add a safety fallback in the batch coordinator to force-bake a batch when no emission occurs for >500ms regardless of estimated occupancy. Owner: Marco Nguyen. Due: 2026-03-20. Status: in development.
2) Medium-term: Rewrite adaptive-window heuristic to be state-machine driven with explicit invariants and timeouts; add a test harness to replay mixed-burst traffic patterns with configurable KV cache hit/miss sequences. Owner: R&D (runtime team) - Priya Sharma. Due: 2026-04-15. Status: planned.
3) Testing: Create a chaos test for the batch formation path that injects timer drift, rapid context-length changes, and cache-hit signals. Integrate into CI gate for runtime-1.x releases. Owner: QA - Daniel Osei. Due: 2026-04-01. Status: in triage.
4) Observability: Add an emission-state metric (enum: idle | waiting | emitting) and expose slot-reservation age histograms and a cohort-level blocked-duration gauge to Console. Owner: Observability - Lena Márquez. Due: 2026-03-28. Status: in progress.
5) Compatibility audit: Review other runtime optimizations that may interact with fallback heuristics (coalescer, KV-cache heuristics, slot-reuse). Produce a short audit doc with recommended safe-guards. Owner: Runtime Arch - Omar El-Hadi. Due: 2026-04-10. Status: planned.
6) Customer communication: Post-incident writeup and targeted outreach to affected customers with remediation timeline and recommended temporary config overrides. Owner: Support - Emily Rosen. Due: 2026-03-18. Status: drafting.

Proposed long-term decisions: 
- Keep a conservative default for the adaptive-window in hosted tier; expose an advanced knob for Dedicated customers who want aggressive latency/throughput tradeoffs.
- Move composite interaction tests into pre-release performance validation for every runtime release.

Relevant artifacts and links:
- Incident dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/incident/ENG-65012
- Rollback PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8392
- Reproducer harness (internal): https://github.com/redwood-inference/load-tests/tree/eng/continuous-batching-repro
- Initial triggered alert & SRE notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/ENG-65012

Open questions for the next triage meeting:
- Should the forced-bake timeout be tenant-configurable? (trade-offs: fairness vs. cost)
- Is the cache-hit fast-path worth the complexity across all model families, or should it be a model-family opt-in?
- Are there other heuristics that rely on the same implicit wake-up ordering?

Conclusion:
This incident highlights the risk of combining multiple micro-optimizations without a compositional test strategy. The immediate rollback resolved customer impact; the next milestones focus on adding defensive fallbacks, improving observability, and expanding test coverage so similar composite regressions are caught earlier in the pipeline.
